newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Scuffles during Cyprus anti-British protest.
newsitem.headline: Scuffles during Cyprus anti-British protest.

text.p: Scuffles broke out and the Union Jack flag was removed from the car of the British High Commissioner in Cyprus during a demonstration on Saturday against British military bases on the island.

Witnesses said the incident occured during the opening ceremony of part of a new motorway linking the southern coastal town of Limassol to the western resort of Paphos. Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides attended the ceremony.
Part of the new motorway runs through the base of Episkopi, one of two bases Britain has retained on the island since Cyprus independence in 1960.
British High Commissioner David Madden told Reuters there was a "small demonstration."
"Yes, they may have removed something but it is not a big issue, it is not a big issue, no," he said when asked if a protester removed the Union Jack from his limousine.
The red-white-and-blue flag was absent from the Jaguar when Madden arrived an hour later at a shipping conference in Limassol.
Marios Matsakis, a member of parliament who witnessed the incident told Reuters bases police "provoked" the demonstrators when they attempted to arrest one of them.

Bases spokesman Mervyn Wynne-Jones denied police had attempted to arrest anybody. "The (bases) police did restrain one or two protesters to prevent them from disrupting procedures but certainly there were no arrests," he said.
Matsakis said he saw the flag being removed from the High Commissioner's car.
"Yes I saw that happening. I don't agree with that," he said.
A recent poll commissioned by the local Periodiko magazine said that some 70 percent of Cypriots believed Britain should close the bases.
